chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Khālid ibn Nāfiʿ al-Bajalī, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who granted another man residence in a house belonging to him for the duration of his life, meaning the life of the owner of the house. Then the one who granted the residence died, while the one to whom the residence had been granted remained alive. Do you think that if the heirs want to remove him from the house, they have that right?

He said: "I hold that the house should be appraised with a fair valuation, and the deceased's one-third should be examined. If in his one-third there is that which covers the value of the house, then the heirs have no right to remove him. But if the one-third does not cover the value of the house, then they have the right to remove him."

It was said to him: "Do you think that if the man to whom the residence was granted dies after the death of the owner of the house, the residence would belong to the descendants of the one to whom the residence was granted?" He said: "No."

key_terms.الدَّارِ: the house or property in which residence was granted
key_terms.الْوَرَثَةُ: the heirs of the deceased owner
key_terms.بِقِيمَةٍ عَادِلَةٍ: with a fair and just valuation
key_terms.ثُلُثِ الْمَيِّتِ: the deceased person's one-third estate portion
key_terms.سُكْنَى: the granted right of residence in a house

ai.seo_question: Does a lifetime residence grant in a house remain valid after the owner's death, and does it pass to the beneficiary's heirs?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling concerning a lifetime right of residence granted in a house. The Imam عليه السلام explains that its enforceability after the owner's death depends on whether the value can be covered from the deceased's one-third estate allocation, and he clarifies that this right of residence does not pass on to the beneficiary's descendants.
